subject: What is the best way to do Kronecker product in Stan? Is writing for loop the only way?

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: What is the best way to do Kronecker product in Stan? Is writing for loop the only way?
parts:
Hi, all,  is there anyway to improve my code's speed?
I'm trying to use Stan to implement my hierarchical model:

y_itkj ~ dpois(n_itkj*p_itkj)


log(p_itkj) = Z_itkj + e_itkj


Zj = Z[ , , , j]


Zj ~ prod(positive eigen values of H) * exp(-1/2 * Z_j' %*% Hj %*% Z_j)


where
Hj = kronecker( kronecker( inverse(Sigma), A), C)

 is an 115*8*2 square matrix, not full rank. Sigma is full rank 2 by 2, A is 8 by 8 but rank=6, C is full rank 115 by 115.

Some details are omitted.

So I other than specifying matrix Hj, all the other parts seem easy to write. However, it took me some efforts to code the kronecker product as in my code shown below.

My question is : is this the only way to perform Kronecker product?

CODE:

data{
  int<lower=1> I;//counties
  int<lower=1> T;//time periods
  int<lower=1> K;//genders
  int<lower=1> J;//age groups
  
  matrix[I,I] Cmatrix;//adjacency matrix
  matrix[I,I] Identity;//Identity matrix
  real max_rho;//upper boundary of rho,to make precision matrix p.d.
  matrix[K,K] W;//prior of SIGMA
  vector[I] lambda;//eigens of Cmatrix
  vector[I*T*K] n[J];//obsed population
  //vector[I*T*K] y[J];//obsed data
  int<lower=0> y[J,I*T*K];
  matrix[T,T] A;//temporal smoothing matrix
}
transformed data{
  int KT;
  KT <- K*T;
}
parameters{
  vector[I*T*K] Z[J];
  vector[I*T*K] V[J];
  matrix[K,K] SIGMA[J];
  real<lower=0> delta0;
  //real<lower=0,upper=max_rho> rho[J];
  real rho[J];
}
transformed parameters{
  matrix[I*T*K,I*T*K] H;
  matrix[I,I] B;
  matrix[K,K] sig_inv;
  matrix[K*T,K*T] first_product;
  matrix[I*K*T,I*K*T] second_product;
  real log_rho[J];
  
  //Calculating Hj
  
  for(j in 1:J){
    B <-  Identity - rho[j]*Cmatrix;
    sig_inv  <-  inverse_spd(SIGMA[j]);
    //first product
    for(d1 in 1:K){
      for(d2 in 1:K){
        for(s1 in 1:T){
          for(s2 in 1:T){
            first_product[(d1-1)*T+s1, (d2-1)*T+s2]<- sig_inv[d1,d2]*A[s1,s2];
          }
        }
        
      }
    }
    //Second product
    for (d1 in 1:KT){
  for (d2 in 1:KT){
  for (s1 in 1:I){
  for (s2 in 1:I){
  second_product[(d1-1)*I+s1, (d2-1)*I+s2]<- first_product[d1,d2]*B[s1,s2];
  }
  }
  }
 }
    H <- second_product;
    log_rho[j] <- sum(1-rho[j]*lambda)*(T-2)*K/2.0-1/2.0*quad_form(H, Z[j]);
  }
  
} 

model{
  delta0 ~ inv_gamma(2.0, 0.005);
  for(j in 1:J){
    rho[j] ~ uniform(0, max_rho);
    SIGMA[j] ~ inv_wishart(2,W);
    increment_log_prob(log_rho[j]);
    V[j] ~ normal(Z[j], delta0);//this can be improved with std normal then transforming
    y[j] ~ poisson_log(log(n[j]+V[j]));
  }
}


If possible, can someone also tell me how to pass R values to the Stan array of vectors? As said in the menu, the array and vectors can't be passed within each other. However, if I'm passing an R object to Stan
matrix[K,K] x[J]
, I'm supposed to pass an R array with dim=c(J,K,K), is that right?
